basic_information.short_title: Official Seal of the Bangsamoro Parliament
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ADOPTING AN OFFICIAL SEAL FOR THE PARLIAMENT OF THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Adopts the Parliament's own official seal — a green circle carrying the Bangsamoro flag on a shield, eighty boxes for the 80 members, and an open book for the rule of law — used to authenticate its acts.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To establish the Parliament as the legislative authority of the region in its own right, with a mark reflective of its functions and of the struggles and aspirations of its people.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Parliament and its members have a seal of their own, distinct from the Bangsamoro Seal, for use on official acts, communications and documents.
who_will_be_affected: Anyone receiving an official document from Parliament or a Member
Members of Parliament, who may use the seal on their own official communications
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2021 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. Parliament has its own seal, separate from the region's. The eighty boxes on it stand for the 80 members, and the open book for adherence to the rule of law.
in_practice: Circular, bordered by two green (#009966) circles
'BANGSAMORO PARLIAMENT' in green on white across the upper portion
'20 BARMM 19' on red (#FF3333) across the lower portion
At the centre, the Bangsamoro flag shaped as a shield, outlined in grey (#C8C8C8)
Eighty green boxes in a horseshoe shape, representing the Parliament's 80 members
An open book in light grey on a brown stand above the shield, for adherence to the rule of law
May be used on all official acts, communications and documents of Parliament and its members, alongside the Official Bangsamoro Seal

for_specific_groups.Anyone verifying a document: Section 3 describes every element with hex codes, so a seal can be checked against the law.
for_specific_groups.Members of Parliament: The seal may be used by members as well as by the institution, as provided in the Parliamentary Rules.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Bangsamoro Parliament and its members.
what_you_can_do: Check an official parliamentary document against the description in Section 3 if its authenticity matters to you
watch_out_for: The act creates no offence for forging or misusing the seal.
Usage is permissive — the seal 'may be used' — with detail left to the Parliamentary Rules.

key_terms_explained.Kris: The wavy-bladed sword; here it represents the struggle for the right to self-determination.
key_terms_explained.Horseshoe: The shape of a parliamentary chamber, formed here by the eighty boxes.
key_terms_explained.20 BARMM 19: The region's year of creation, split across the lower band of the seal.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed 19 January 2021, approved by the Chief Minister on 12 February 2021.

Someone checking a document can compare the seal against Section 3, which gives the exact colours and every symbol's meaning.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Adopts an Official Seal for the Bangsamoro Parliament, for authentication in the exercise of its acts and other purposes.

Section 2 — Policy: in exercising its right to self-governance the region adopts a seal for the Parliament, establishing it as the legislative authority of the BARMM in recognition of the justness and legitimacy of the cause of the Bangsamoro people, reflective of its functions and of the struggles and aspirations of its people.

Section 3 — Design: circular, with two green (#009966) lines forming the outer and inner borders; 'BANGSAMORO PARLIAMENT' in the same green on white (#FFFFFF) in the upper portion, and '20 BARMM 19' on red (#FF3333) in the lower portion. At the centre of the inner circle is the BARMM flag shaped as a shield outlined in grey (#C8C8C8), surrounded by eighty boxes representing the Bangsamoro Parliament, in green, formed in a horseshoe shape. The Kris represents the struggle for the right to self-determination; the Crescent represents moral governance; the Star represents the component provinces, cities and geographic areas composing the BARMM; Crescent and Star together represent the BARMM. An open book in light grey (#EAEAEA, #D3D3D3) on a brown (#391C0C, #592912) stand, signifying the living adherence of the Parliament to the rule of law, sits above the shield.

Section 4 — The seal may be used in all official acts, communications and other documents of the Parliament and its members, alongside the Official Bangsamoro Seal, as may be provided in the Parliamentary Rules, Procedures and Practices.
Section 5 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a regional newspaper of general circulation.

related_legislation.related_note: The fourth of the symbols acts, after the flag (BAA 1), the emblem or Bangsamoro Seal (BAA 2) and the hymn (BAA 7). Unlike BAA 2, this one specifies its colours by hex code.

citizen_questions.a: They represent the Bangsamoro Parliament — the Bangsamoro Transition Authority has 80 members — arranged in a horseshoe, the shape of a parliamentary chamber.

citizen_questions.q: What does the open book mean?
citizen_questions.a: Section 3 says it signifies the living adherence of the Parliament to the rule of law.

citizen_questions.q: Is this the same as the Bangsamoro Seal?
citizen_questions.a: No. This is Parliament's own seal. Section 4 says it may be used alongside the Official Bangsamoro Seal adopted by BAA 2.

citizen_questions.q: Can a Member of Parliament use it?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. Section 4 covers official acts, communications and documents of the Parliament and its members.
